ev_022a41f4e2f6.description: While preserving her musical past, vocalist and kora player Sona Jobarteh innovates to support a more humanitarian future. The spirit of Jobarteh's musical work stands on the mighty shoulders of the West African Griot tradition; she is a living archive of the Gambian people. With one ear on her family's historic reputation, one on its future legacy, and her heart in both places, she is preparing a path for the next generation. Jobarteh's dedication to spreading powerful humanitarian messages through her songs and her stage performances makes her much more than a musician; she is active in social change and leads by her own example. Jobarteh single-handedly set up The Gambia Academy: a pioneering institution dedicated to achieving educational reform across the continent of Africa. This academy is the first of its kind to deliver a mainstream academic curriculum at a high level, while also focusing on the culture, traditions, and history that belong to its students. These efforts have gained her invitations to deliver speeches at high profile events around the world, including summits for the UN, the World Trade Organization, and UNICEF. Publisher Marina Lazzara hosts. Each morning Danny Rosen pees on the bank of the largest unnamed tributary to the East Branch of Big Salt Wash which flows into the Colorado River several miles below Fruita, Colorado. Early on he learned to swing a hammer and that changed everything. He has been a poet, publisher, teacher, geologist, astronomer, and carpenter. In the middle of his journey he found himself running an astronomical observatory in the heart of the Namib Desert under the southern sky where he cultivated an optimistic outlook based on his familiarity with big space and deep time. He is the author of Suspended Erosion (2024), The Tuscan Journals & Other Poems (2022), Primate Poems (2016), Ghosts of Giant Kudu (2013), and That Curve (2006). He founded Lithic Press in 2007 and has run Lithic Bookstore since its opening in 2015. An inveterate rock hanger, he has collaborated with beavers on a variety of landscape installations. The Dolphins Quartet is a string quartet and composer collective united by a belief that chamber music can be vibrant, daring, and deeply human. Trained at Juilliard and based in New York City, the quartet has gained recognition for adventurous programming, original compositions, and performances that reimagine the possibilities of quartet playing. In April 2026, they won Gold Prize and Audience Prize at the Chesapeake Chamber Music Competition, establishing their presence as a world-class ensemble in the classical music scene. Read more here! Eddie Henderson , Cecil McBee , George Cables , and Billy Hart all came up in the heady era of the mid-60s as members of some of the most important bands of the era. Hart and Henderson were members of Herbie Hancock's groundbreaking Mwandishi group; Cecil McBee anchored Charles Lloyd's great '60s quartet alongside Keith Jarrett and Jack DeJohnette; while Cables held down the piano chair in numerous bands including groups led by Sonny Rollins, Joe Henderson, Freddie Hubbard, Dexter Gordon and Art Pepper. David Weiss , Donald Harrison , and Azar Lawrence , from a more recent generation, are experts in this forthright lingo, having gained experience performing with Art Blakey, Bobby Hutcherson, Freddie Hubbard, Charles Tolliver, Roy Haynes and Herbie Hancock. Sung's "Oracles Quartet" distills this music for small group, while including the music of a living oracle (or two) as well. ARTIST BIO: Described as "one of the most exciting new pianist-composers of her generation" (Qobuz) with "piano playing at a quite unbelievably jaw-dropping level" (London Jazz News), Helen Sung is a dazzling story-teller at her instrument, moving listeners with her passion and inspired creativity. Like a hip-hop link up from the 90s, the pair's collective ear, musical talents, and friendship pushes the limits of the R&B organ trio sound into a youthful, tasty style of 'blue collar jazz.' Fonville x Fribush features a rotating cast of guitarists in the studio, including Charlie Hunter, Alan Good Parker and Morgan Burrs. Songs like "I Couldn't Love You More" and "Blue Chips" immerse audiences in Atlantic Coast soundscapes of their hometown roots in North Carolina and Virginia. In 2026, they released their debut Fonville x Fribush EP, R&B Organ Trio , featuring Charlie Hunter. Opera Parallèle presents TAKING UP SERPENTS by Composer Kamala Sankaram and Librettist Jerre Dye Every family has its gospel. Making its West Coast debut, Taking Up Serpents is a riveting chamber opera exploring faith, family, and the beliefs that shape us. Featuring a folk-inspired score by acclaimed composer Kamala Sankaram—hailed by The Washington Post as "one of the most exciting composers in the country"—and a libretto by Jerre Dye, the opera follows a young woman's reluctant return home after her estranged preacher father is bitten by one of his own snakes. With a striking new production directed and conceived by Brian Staufenbiel. Nicole Paiement conducts the definitive version of the score, featuring an exceptional Bay Area cast. This is a reserved seating show. You will be given the option to select your seat assignment and the price point upon booking. Content Note TAKING UP SERPENTS Includes mature themes and simulated stage violence. Ticketing Policies Ticket purchases are non-refundable. We follow a young woman named Anya, who remembers almost nothing of her past, as she joins a quick-thinking con man and a former aristocrat on a journey to Paris to convince the Dowager Empress that Anya is her long-lost granddaughter. With a Soviet officer on their trail and fragments of memory beginning to surface, Anya must face a question she never expected: what if the story they have rehearsed is her own? Stanford's vocalists and instrumentalists present Anastasia, the 2016 musical inspired by the beloved 1997 animated film, a story about who we become when the past goes missing. Directed by Ariela Morgenstern, with Musical Director Marie-Louise Catsalis and Vocal Director Benjamin Liupaogo. The Santa Clara Historic Train Depot, Bluegrass, Country, Old Time, & Folk jam is free and open to intermediate and experienced stringed instrument players. The jam started in 2012, and is now on its 11th year. The The South Bay Historic Railroad Society kindly lends chairs and space for the jam. ev_104f2c9ec683.description: The Garage Jam is an open, friendly bluegrass circle that meets the first and third Monday of every month, from 6 to 8 pm. All kinds of pickers show up, from rank beginners to grizzled veterans, plus folks who just come to listen and socialize. The repertoire is straight-up traditional bluegrass, although the occasional old-time or folk-inflected choice will pop up. The format is the old-fashioned song circle, with each participant getting a turn to call a song and set its key, pace, and feel. An experienced jam leader and bass player are always present to help keep things on track. Everyone is welcome — come on down!

ev_1354916f77bd.description: Founded by Fattah Abbou and Mohamed Aoualou , AZA unites traditional Tamazight (incorrectly labeled "Berber") music, indigenous to North Africa, with the global influences of its diverse members. With elements of indigenous Moroccan musical styles, including Ahwash, Rwais, and Gnawa – among others – AZA's stirring performances feature deep, danceable rhythms, intricate melodies, and soaring, soulful vocals. Visually dynamic and engaging performers, AZA has been inspiring international audiences for more than 20 years. Fattah Abbou is native to Morocco (Imazighen), where he played and studied music for over thirty-five years, and is recognized as a master musician. Fattah formed AZA in Santa Cruz, California with former member Mohamed Aoualou, after moving to the United States over twenty years ago. The unique exchange between Morocco and Californian musicians has proved potent; AZA has produced four albums of original compositions, and performed at music festivals, clubs, and universities around the United States and abroad. ev_149b4ec4929b.description: The Garage Jam is an open, friendly bluegrass circle that meets the first and third Monday of every month, from 6 to 8 pm. All kinds of pickers show up, from rank beginners to grizzled veterans, plus folks who just come to listen and socialize. The repertoire is straight-up traditional bluegrass, although the occasional old-time or folk-inflected choice will pop up. The format is the old-fashioned song circle, with each participant getting a turn to call a song and set its key, pace, and feel. An experienced jam leader and bass player are always present to help keep things on track. Everyone is welcome — come on down!

ev_1f2d8e91b4b9.description: Take a comfy seat and celebrate the grand finale of SF Stairway Month hearing authors Mary Burk (Stairway Walks in San Francisco) and Alexandra Kenin (Urban Trails series, San Francisco, East Bay, Peninsula and South Bay). And sharpen your wits: We will have special SF stairway trivia game designed by moderator Liz Novoa (aka Instagram's staircase queen). Mary and Alex will delight you with stories of SF's known and hidden stairways, tell you about the best views, and share the whereabouts of secret gardens and more. Mary enjoyed a longstanding partnership with Adah Bakalinsky, co-authoring these now renowned stairway books until Adah's passing at over 100 years old. Alex is the embodiment of energy. In addition to highlights from her book(s), she will share her detailed map of everything that you have wanted to know about SF's roughly1000 stairways. This event is organized by Glen Park Beautiful (www.gpbeautiful.org). It is the 3rd annual SF Stairway Month, which was inspired by the creation of Glen Park's Burnside Tiled Steps. The event is also featured in this inaugural year of Walktober, a month-long celebration of guided walks in San Francisco hosted by the Crosstown Trail .

ev_1f3afe7493b6.description: The Django Festival All-Stars have grown into a brilliantly cohesive group of musicians who've taken the world by storm, performing at top concert halls and festivals to packed houses and standing ovations. The group's music speaks of Paris in the 1920s and 1930s, when "gitane" music filled the air, in the cafés, the streets, in the countryside, a romantic Paris with lovers, campfires, a time of Montmartre, la belle époque, le Boudon café, café au lait, luscious pastry, and a great glass of wine. Django Reinhardt was "king" – teaming with violinist Stephane Grappelli and making musical history. The Django Festival Allstars bring this music into the current day, combining known standards and original music in an intoxicating way. They swing like crazy and will break your heart with a ballad. Bridgewater's career has always bridged musical genres. She earned her first professional experience as a member of the legendary Thad Jones/Mel Louis Big Band, and throughout the '70s she performed with such jazz notables as Max Roach, Sonny Rollins, Dexter Gordon, and Dizzy Gillespie. After a foray into the pop world during the 1980s, she relocated to Paris and began to turn her attention back to jazz. Signing with Universal Music Group as a producer (Bridgewater produces all of her albums), Bridgewater released a series of critically acclaimed titles beginning with Keeping Tradition in 1993. All but one – including her wildly successful double GRAMMY Award-winning tribute to Ella Fitzgerald, Dear Ella – have received GRAMMY nominations. This first-time collaboration includes ... Kathy Kallick (guitar) and Bethany Sorkey (bass) from the Good Ol' Persons ... Kathy, Greg Booth (dobro), & Tom Bekeny (mandolin) from the Kathy Kallick Band ... and jam enthusiasts Bethany, Tom, and Larry Chung (anything with strings). All five are beloved teachers throughout the west coast. Expect some classic bluegrass and country, swing, Kathy originals, and more in what promises to be a compelling blend of experience and spontaneity.

ev_267726303eda.description: Kurt Rosenwinkel is a highly acclaimed and influential jazz guitarist, composer, and bandleader. Hailed as one of the most important jazz musicians of his generation, Rosenwinkel has spent decades pushing the boundaries of the jazz genre and developing a signature sound that has captivated audiences worldwide. With a career spanning over thirty years, Rosenwinkel has released a series of groundbreaking albums, collaborated with jazz legends, and continues to inspire the next generation of jazz musicians. Gerald Clayton suggests a new ideal and a promising way forward in modern jazz. A pianist, composer, and seven-time GRAMMY nominee, he stands out for his ability to balance heritage and innovation; bridging the tradition he grew up in and a fearless sense of exploration. As a bandleader, he's created music that ranges from the intimate reflections of Bells on Sand to the electrifying immediacy of Happening: Live at the Village Vanguard . Together, Kurt Rosenwinkel and Gerald Clayton present a very special evening guitar-piano duets. Kurt Rosenwinkel Website Gerald Clayton Website Sponsored by Rosalind & Howard Fisher (Ticket Includes 5% City of Santa Cruz Admission Tax) .embed-cont

ev_2894cc6b65c6.description: Gabrielle Cavassa is a singer and composer from Escondido, California. She was ushered into the spotlight through her collaboration with renowned saxophonist Joshua Redman on his 2023 record where are we . In a five-star album review by DownBeat , Cavassa is hailed as "a young singer with a deep, rich, and fragile voice...a star in the making." Cavassa began "obsessively listening" to records from a young age. Largely self-taught, she developed a unique approach to singing that would later characterize her artistry. Cavassa received a Bachelor of Arts in Music from San Francisco State University, but credits the Bay Area music scene for her "real education." In 2020, Cavassa independently released an eponymous debut record produced by collaborator Jamison Ross. In 2021, she was crowned a winner of the prestigious International Sarah Vaughan Jazz Vocal Competition. Later that year she was discovered by Redman's manager at an event in New Orleans, leading to their collaboration on the 2023 record. ev_296af491eefb.description: On this rare concert date, Vijay Iyer and Wadada Leo Smith revisit the music from their collaborative albums – 2016's A Cosmic Rhythm With Each Stroke, and 2025's Defiant Life – for this evening of duets. Of Defiant Life , Pitchfork writes that "The second collaborative album by the jazz composers and instrumentalists is a searching meditation on resistance and revolutionary potential." Described by The New York Times as a "social conscience, multimedia collaborator, system builder, rhapsodist, historical thinker and multicultural gateway," Vijay Iyer has carved out a unique path as an influential, prolific, shape-shifting presence in twenty-first century music. A composer and pianist active and revered across multiple musical communities, Iyer has created a consistently innovative, emotionally resonant body of work over the last three decades, earning him a place as one of the leading music-makers of his generation. Iyer's musical language is indebted to the great composer-pianists from Duke Ellington to Alice Coltrane, the rhythmic traditions of South Asia and West Africa, and the African American creative music movement of the sixties and seventies. Dr. Calloway has also had a long career as a leading educator in Latin jazz and Cuban music, directing the Afro-Cuban ensemble of San Francisco State University and the Latin Jazz Youth Ensemble of San Francisco. ev_2d96d87856a4.description: Lucía is a 24-year-old vocalist from Veracruz, México whose singular artistic vision bridges the gaps between jazz, latin, and pop music. Lucía Gutierrez Rebolloso started her musical career at the age of two, singing and dancing in her parents' son jarocho band, Son de Madera. She began studying voice at the age of thirteen at Universidad Veracruzana, and in 2022 received a Bachelor's degree in Jazz Studies from this same university. In 2022, she became the first artist from Mexico to enter the Sarah Vaughan International Jazz Vocal Competition, which she won. Lucía has already collaborated with several world-renowned artists and musicians, including Natalia Lafourcade, Aloe Blacc, La Santa Cecilia, Quetzal, Son de Madera, Alex Mercado, and the National Jazz Orchestra of Mexico. Most recently, Lucía has just released her first full album. Produced by GRAMMY-winner Matt Pierson, it presents Lucía's interpretations of jazz standards (such as "What a Difference a Day Makes" and "You Must Believe in Spring") classic Spanish songs (including "Silencio" and "La Llorona") and current pop songs. Lucía Website Sponsored by Monica and David Terrazas (Ticket Includes 5% City of Santa Cruz Ad

ev_2e4c109e774c.description: Michael Mayo leans on his intuition as a vocalist, composer, songwriter, and arranger. Much like molding and shaping a sculpture out of clay, he stretches his voice through layers of heavenly harmonizing, hard-hitting beatboxing, and heartfelt crooning. The Los Angeles-based phenomenon creates from the heart without filter or pretense, allowing his voice to transmit raw emotion above an ever-evolving backdrop of jazz, neo-soul, and R&B on his second full-length LP, Fly , and more to come. "As improvisers, we sometimes talk about leaving space and following your second or third instinct," Mayo notes. "Lately, I've been trying to challenge myself by going with my first instinct and seeing what sticks. Fly has been a fun experiment in that...To me, this album feels very, 'Let's go.'" For this concert they're joined by special guest Simon Planting on bass. Their music draws equally from European jazz, Eastern European folk influences, and classic vocal jazz, resulting in a sound that feels both timeless and accessible to modern audiences. A defining element of their collaboration is the integration of vocals. In addition to her virtuosic violin playing, Eva incorporates scat singing and vocal improvisation in a subtle, musical style reminiscent of George Benson. At times she sings while playing, adding a distinctive and engaging layer that resonates strongly with jazz audiences. Their repertoire includes French chanson, swing standards, and original arrangements that evoke travel, nostalgia, and joy. ev_30d7cb5b66a0.description: An evening of new music for stringed traditional East Asian instruments. Featuring Katherine Whatley (koto and voice), Southeast of Rain (pipa, voice, electronics), and Stella Da Yun Song (haegeum). About the performers and pieces: Katherine Whatley Katherine Whatley is a koto musician, composer, and PhD Candidate in East Asian Languages and Cultures at Stanford University. She plays both traditional and experimental koto, both improvised and composed. Her compositions have been performed by the Stanford New Ensemble and the Earplay Ensemble. She has performed in a variety of contexts including at the Good Shepherd Center (Seattle), Columbia University (New York), on tour across Japan and in Berlin. Her dissertation analyzes music and soundscape in medieval Japanese literature. Her research has previously been published in The February Journal, positions, Japanese Journal of Religious Studies, and Migrating Minds. As a journalist, she has worked with the BBC, Dwell, Conde Nast, New York Times, the Japan Times, and others. 今、箏ひびき(Ima Koto Hibiki)—Now, Here Koto Sings This piece for 13-string koto and voice is based on Ryōjin Hisho, a 12th-century collection of imayō (popular songs).

ev_33aaf59551de.description: The Washington Post exclaims, "Kandace Springs' voice is undeniable. It's one of those generational voices; from the first note, you know it's special." Pianist and singer Kandace Springs ' natural gifts for lyricism and soulfulness have earned her recognition as one of the premier female artists of the jazz/soul genre. Described as having "a voice that could melt snow" by her late mentor Prince, the Nashville native has racked up an impressive list of accomplishments, from national TV appearances, headlining major jazz festivals, and collaborations with such luminaries as Christian McBride and Norah Jones. Springs' 2024 release, Run Your Race, was a tribute to her late father, legendary Nashville soul singer Scat Springs, and was the first album of hers to feature almost all original songs. Prior to that, in 2020, Kandace released The Women Who Raised Me , garnering five-star reviews from publications ranging from DownBeat to The New Yorker . Springs looks forward to celebrating more of music's greatest icons with the release of The Women Who Raised Me Vol. II in 2027. ev_373a470c5987.description: BMG PRESENTS | BMG PRESENTS TUESDAY MARCH 2ND — TREVER M. KEITH & LILLY HIATT — DOORS 7:00 PM / SHOW 8:00 PM ADVANCE TICKETS AVAILABLE — IVY ROOM 860 San Pablo Ave, Albany • 21+ — TREVER M. KEITH — In truth, there will be a lot of intrigue sparked when music freaks and the curious alike find out Trever M. Keith, storied founder and front man for pioneering So Cal punk band Face to Face, is putting out an Americana album. "When I really started thinking about it, there's a lot more country in my background than I actually realized," the 57-year-old says. ev_3ee4a4c76c3b.description: Born and raised in Madrid, Spain, pianist and composer Marta Sánchez is actively working in the contemporary creative music scene in New York City and around the globe. Charting a significant path through her innovative and original music, she has reached an international audience and gained significant global recognition. Sánchez, the 2025 DownBeat Critics Poll 'Rising Star' in piano, leads a quintet on this concert date featuring Devon Gates on vocals, Alex LoRe on alto saxophone, Roman Filiu on tenor saxophone, Rashaan Carter on bass, and Allan Mednard on drums. The group has released five albums, two of them selected by The New York Times among the ten best records of their respective release years. Sánchez is currently presenting the music of her latest album, Shamanism , in which she expands the quintet with vocals, combining her music with lyrics that address often-unspoken experiences, including depression, infertility, and ageism, among others. ev_3fd3b077d537.description: "Raw, underground, and chaotic...one of modern jazz music's most audacious futurists." – Pitchfork Revered by living icons and underground tastemakers, Kassa Overall began his career behind the drum kit. At the Oberlin Conservatory of Music, Overall spent his days studying jazz drums and music theory, and his evenings making beats in his dorm room, often staying home from parties to pull all-nighters in front of his MPC, studio monitors, and an open Pro Tools session. At Oberlin, he met musicians who remain his closest musical collaborators to this day. Overall's groundbreaking solo projects have established him as a driving force on the international stage, fielding support from visionaries including Thom Yorke, Iggy Pop, Virgil Abloh, and more. His first studio album, GO GET ICE CREAM AND LISTEN TO JAZZ (2019) bore witness to the emergence of a sound that layered the virtuosic drumming, polyrhythmic rapping, and meticulous production techniques he had honed separately. On 2020's I THINK I'M GOOD , his voice continued to crystallize, critiquing the injustices of the carceral system, the pharmaceutical industry, and anti-black racism. With ANIMALS , released in 2023 on Warp Records

ev_4286a05dfc3e.description: Kim Shuck conducts the twice-monthly Virtual Poets series, with featured readers followed by an open mic on the 2nd Monday of each month and an all-open mic session on the 4th Monday of each month. Kim embraces the fool and jester qualities of being a modern poet and artist. She is a devotee of San Francisco, whose hills she wanders nearly always on foot. Her maternal grandparents met at the Polish Hall on Shotwell and she spent many hours with her mother and grandmother wandering the Mission St. Miracle Mile, taking books out of the Mission Branch library and watching aquarium fish on the ground floor of what used to be Hale's. She firmly believes in carrying a bubble wand, keys, pen and notebook and cats cradle string at all times. Kim, whose poetry draws on her multiethnic background which includes Polish and Cherokee heritage, and her experiences as a lifelong resident of San Francisco, served as San Francisco's seventh Poet Laureate, from 2017-2021. In 2019, she was awarded an inaugural National Laureate Fellowship from the Academy of American Poets, and a PEN Oakland Censorship Award. Among her many books and chapbooks, Pick a Garnet to Sleep In , one in a long line of poetry

ev_43cb5127d7c0.description: Ella Dair is a NYC-based jazz vocalist. Originally from San Francisco, she started singing at a young age, performing with many Bay Area legends in her aunt's swing band "Lavay Smith & Her Red Hot Skillet Lickers." Ella continued her education in music and performance with SFArtsEd, falling in love with the songs of Harold Arlen and Kander & Ebb, among other classics of the Great American Songbook. As a teenager she was a vocal soloist with the youth choir at Glide Memorial, the renowned non-denominational church presided over by civil rights leader Cecil Williams. Ella earned her bachelor's degree from Bard College, studying anthropology and Latin American studies with a particular interest in ethnomusicology. Her studies broadened her musical tastes and sent her to Mexico City, where she lived post-grad. Ella then moved to New York City, joining the staff at Dizzy's Club at Jazz At Lincoln Center, where she has been exposed to many of the greatest jazz musicians in the world. On her regular trips to the West Coast Ella performs at The Royal Cuckoo Organ Lounge in San Francisco, an iconic institution that has received rave reviews from the New York Times and the San Francisco Chro

The Santa Clara Historic Train Depot, Bluegrass, Country, Old Time, & Folk jam is free and open to intermediate and experienced stringed instrument players. The jam started in 2012, and is now on its 11th year. The The South Bay Historic Railroad Society kindly lends chairs and space for the jam. The jam takes place on the patio on sunny days in front of the historic depot and train museum. When the weather is inclement, the jam moves into the train museum. Parking is free in front of the depot museum, $5.50 if you park in the caltran parking lot.

His playing and composing are rooted in the jazz tradition, occasionally extending into classical, folk, and experimental influences. Rogers has performed nationwide at venues such as Dizzy's Club, Nublu, SFJAZZ, The Sound Room, and LIBRETTO, and at festivals including the Vail Jazz Festival, Charles River Jazz Festival, Concord Jazz Festival, and West Oakland Sound Series. As a composer, Rogers has had works premiered by professional chamber ensembles, including HYPERCUBE and resident performers at New Music On The Point . In 2024, he was awarded a Flint Initiative Grant to compose and record EIGHT VIGNETTES for alto saxophone, which premiered in February 2025. ev_46a325042b09.description: THE STELLA HEATH CHRISTMAS SHOW – Billie Holiday/ Ella Fitzgerald Tribute! This special performance will be a heartfelt homage to ELLA FITZGERALD the First Lady of Song, blending her timeless music with fascinating historical stories and meticulous research. Stella and her quintet will also present the music of BILLIE HOLIDAY. Shrouded in mystery as she was draped in fur, Billie was multi-faceted; she possessed a sensitivity and ability to make the songs she sang as personal as if she was singing them softly in your very own ear. Featuring some of the Bay Area's finest Jazz musicians, Stella's quintet brings back the electric and intimate feeling of seeing Lady Day live in a 1930's Jazz Club.

Fumi Tomita, bass Carl Clements, woodwinds Jason Ennis, guitars Gary Fieldman, drums Fumi Tomita is a jazz bassist, composer, educator, and author. His newest recording, Yokai! Songs of the Japanese Supernatural will be released in October 2026 on Origin records and was inspired by 19th-century woodblock prints of Yokai and other Japanese supernatural creatures derived from folklore. The album will be supported by a Northeast tour during October and November. His 2020 release Celebrating Bird: The Music of Charlie Parker was similarly received. Tomita was active on the New York city jazz scene for over fifteen years and has performed at venues all over the U.S. and Canada including recent appearances at the International Society of Bassists Conference in Ann Harbor, Michigan in June 2023 and the Jazz Education Network conference in New Orleans and a short tour of Georgia, both in Janua

ev_490541862f7a.description: Paul Hanson, reeds; Joel Harrison, guitar; Michael Manring, bass; Scott Amendola, drums Former Berkeley resident, guitarist Joel Harrison, returns to the Bay Area to journey into Miles Davis' iconic 1970 record, "In a Silent Way." The band consists of old allies, some of the Bay Area's finest and most creative musicians—they will also perform some of Harrison's original music. Harrison recently released a live record from the Big Ears Festival of this music. The band's approach will be to "make it new." Guitarist, composer, arranger, lyricist, writer, educator and vocalist Joel Harrison has "created a new blueprint for jazz" (New Orleans Times-Picayune). He has released 27 records, a body of work that connects multiple American traditions. While rooted in jazz, his music moves fluidly through classical, rock, country, and American roots music. The New York Times has described his work as "protean... brilliant." Harrison is the founder and director of the Alternative Guitar Summit, an annual festival devoted to innovative and unconventional guitar music. The Summit has featured artists such as Fred Frith, Nels Cline, Bill Frisell, Julian Lage, Michael Gregory Jackson, Mary Halvorson

ev_49ee9b2a2593.description: The Garage Jam is an open, friendly bluegrass circle that meets the first and third Monday of every month, from 6 to 8 pm. All kinds of pickers show up, from rank beginners to grizzled veterans, plus folks who just come to listen and socialize. The repertoire is straight-up traditional bluegrass, although the occasional old-time or folk-inflected choice will pop up. The format is the old-fashioned song circle, with each participant getting a turn to call a song and set its key, pace, and feel. An experienced jam leader and bass player are always present to help keep things on track. Everyone is welcome — come on down!

The Los Angeles Times named him "one of the top jazz pianists in the world" and Jazz Weekly calls him "The most lyrical piano player of our time." The Philadelphia native started playing professionally as a teenager with Mel Melvin's orchestra and Philly Joe Jones. He moved to New York City at nineteen and freelanced with Roy Haynes, Lee Morgan and James Moody, after the tenor saxophonist heard him play at the Five Spot. Upon Moody's recommendation Dizzy Gillespie hired Barron in 1962 without even hearing him play a note. It was in Dizzy's band where Barron developed an appreciation for Latin and Caribbean rhythms. Written by Franz Kafka Directed by Shafer Mazow and Vanessa Flores Chacko On the morning of his thirtieth birthday, bank officer Josef K. wakes to find strange officials in his room informing him he is under arrest. For what, he doesn't know; and seemingly neither do they. Join us for chapter one of Franz Kafka's absurdist masterpiece, The Trial , an unnervingly timely portrait of man lost in a maze of bureaucracy, silent neighbors, paperwork, and officials who are always simply "following procedure." The Santa Clara Historic Train Depot, Bluegrass, Country, Old Time, & Folk jam is free and open to intermediate and experienced stringed instrument players. The jam started in 2012, and is now on its 11th year. The The South Bay Historic Railroad Society kindly lends chairs and space for the jam. The jam takes place on the patio on sunny days in front of the historic depot and train museum. When the weather is inclement, the jam moves into the train museum. Parking is free in front of the depot museum, $5.50 if you park in the caltran parking lot.

ev_55f25ffc10f7.description: Delbert Anderson , a Diné jazz trumpet artist, composer, and educator, stands at the forefront of a vibrant Native American jazz scene. His work, deeply rooted in his Diné heritage, seamlessly integrates Navajo "spinning songs" of love, healing, and courtship with jazz and funk. With his Delbert Anderson Quartet, Anderson revives the improvised sounds of the Diné circle, blending them with jazz, funk, and hip-hop. His compositions are inspired by Navajo Nation landscapes, historical events, and the desire to preserve and educate about Diné history. This evening will be celebrating Anderson's recent album Live at Kuumbwa Jazz , recorded on our stage. Anderson's other notable projects include "The Long Walk: 1,674 Days," a poignant composition reflecting on a critical period in Navajo history. His commitment to community and education is evident through his "Build A Band" educational program, which teaches jazz improvisation to young students through a Diné and family curriculum, wellness programs, and community outreach initiatives aimed at evoking change for the well-being of all humans. ev_563acd5e6404.description: Hailed as "the future of guitar," Alex Misko is a modern fingerstyle guitar prodigy who mesmerizes audiences worldwide. From viral videos with over 80 million views to performing at Carnegie Hall and collaborating with Hans Zimmer, his music captivates fans online and at live shows around the globe. Still in his 20s, Misko has gained international recognition with seven albums, a YouTube channel exceeding a million subscribers, and performances spanning from America to Japan. He's known for his innovative Frankenstein Guitar, a one-of-a-kind acoustic instrument featuring a triple detuning system, built-in percussion, and 14 pickups. With a style that blends technical innovation with accessible musicality, Misko's compositions transcend cultural barriers and speak a universal language wherever they are heard. A must-see for fans of instrumental brilliance, next-level guitar playing, and world-class musical storytelling. ev_56fd2d696699.description: Home for the Holidays – An Irish Christmas, is a heartwarming, festive celebration that brings the joyous spirit of a traditional Irish house party to life. It captures the deep sense of community and tradition that defines an Irish Christmas. The production blends dazzling instrumental tunes—jigs, reels, and hornpipes—with moving, soulful renditions of traditional Irish Christmas carols and contemporary holiday favorites. Led by Dublin-born pianist and singer-songwriter Eamonn Flynn , the show features the traditional folk quartet, Dublinesque, delivering a vibrant blend of fiery instrumental prowess, storytelling, and classic seasonal melodies. Flynn is joined by Félim Egan on accordion and bodhran, Darcy Noonan on fiddle and vocals and Hector Bragado on Irish banjo and guitar. Adding to the spectacle, dancer Madeline Donnelly from the Kennelly School of Irish Dance will bring the performance to life with thrilling, traditional footwork. Come get into the Christmas spirit with an unforgettable, high-energy experience that feels less like a concert and more like sitting in a cozy, music-filled Irish living room on Christmas Eve. ev_57cf0eab1e02.description: Meshell Ndegeocello's first two Blue Note albums – The Omnichord Real Book (2023) and No More Water: The Gospel Of James Baldwin (2024) – have persuasively reasserted her status as an unparalleled force in modern music, earning her the first two GRAMMY Awards to honor her own albums in her three-decade long recording career; exploding any remaining notions of genre boundaries, and coalescing a tight-knit creative circle that operates collectively in the spirit of their motto: Meshell Ndegeocello is a band. With her latest album, Synonym , Ndegeocello reaches even higher to deliver one of the most ambitious projects in her impressive discography by expanding her cast of collaborators to include an astounding rollcall of featured guests. At its core, the album captures her ingenuity in reimagining and reconceptualizing songs written and performed by other musicians. Exploring expressions of desire, care, heartbreak, friendship, disappointment, and love in all forms, this thoughtfully curated collection of covers ranges from '60s folk and '70s soul, country, and pop to '80s R&B and electro-boogie, early '90s alternative rock, and early aughts hip-hop. ev_5811f4e5fea0.description: Ettore Buzzini's fresh take on bluegrass draws from romantic classical music and rock, and has won him awards and gigs with Del McCoury and Leftover Salmon. Come hear an 18-year old born in an Italian-speaking area of Switzerland who has something to add to American music. Imagine if Earl Scruggs, Eddie Van Halen, and Lord Byron got together for a collab: it might sound something like young Swiss-American songwriting and banjo prodigy Ettore Buzzini's unique sound. To the casual listener, Ettore's might be mistaken for simply hard-driving Bluegrass. But anyone who listens a little more closely will quickly notice that Ettore's virtuosic music blends the iconic acoustic sounds of Americana, youthful energy and hard drive of pop-rock, and, most forcefully, the epic, soul-stirring, romantic emotions of classical music. Ettore will be playing both classics and some new music from his forthcoming album Blue Blue Blue. You can hear some of his music and learn more about him at his website: https://ettorebuzzini.com/home

ev_584ddd7aa200.description: Pianist and two-time GRAMMY nominee Christian Sands is an emerging jazz force. His abundant piano technique perfectly matches his ambition, accomplishing a much deeper musical goal: a fresh look at the entire spectrum of jazz. A protégé of Dr. Billy Taylor, Sands released his debut album at the age of twelve. He came to wider prominence through his work as a member of two bands led by iconic bassist Christian McBride: the Christian McBride Trio and Inside Straight. Sands has shared the stage with such jazz luminaries as Wynton Marsalis, Dianne Reeves, and Sheila E, among many others. Sands is celebrating the release of Christmas Stories , his first album of holiday both songs old and new. While Sands views Christmas as a time of nostalgia, reflection and reunion, he also recognizes it as a time for renewal and looking ahead. Christmas Stories is Sands' fifth release for Mack Avenue, following Reach (2017), Facing Dragons (2018), the GRAMMY-nominated Be Water (2020), and Embracing Dawn (2023). ev_5ad8674474af.description: Kim Shuck conducts the twice-monthly Virtual Poets series, with featured readers followed by an open mic on the 2nd Monday of each month and an all-open mic session on the 4th Monday of each month. Kim embraces the fool and jester qualities of being a modern poet and artist. She is a devotee of San Francisco, whose hills she wanders nearly always on foot. Her maternal grandparents met at the Polish Hall on Shotwell and she spent many hours with her mother and grandmother wandering the Mission St. Miracle Mile, taking books out of the Mission Branch library and watching aquarium fish on the ground floor of what used to be Hale's. She firmly believes in carrying a bubble wand, keys, pen and notebook and cats cradle string at all times. Kim, whose poetry draws on her multiethnic background which includes Polish and Cherokee heritage, and her experiences as a lifelong resident of San Francisco, served as San Francisco's seventh Poet Laureate, from 2017-2021. In 2019, she was awarded an inaugural National Laureate Fellowship from the Academy of American Poets, and a PEN Oakland Censorship Award. Among her many books and chapbooks, Pick a Garnet to Sleep In , one in a long line of poetry

ev_5ca29de2f109.description: "A Brazilian-born genius with a blistering voice" ( JazzTimes ), Rio-born and GRAMMY-nominated Claudia Villela has developed a reputation as a singularly unique singer, pianist and composer, lending her five-octave voice to work with jazz luminaries including Kenny Werner, Michael Brecker and Toots Thielemans. Villela began singing professionally as a teen and eventually moved to the Bay Area. A scholarship to New York's Manhattan School of Music and studies with the legendary Sheila Jordan cemented Villela's jazz credentials, and she returned to California as an artist on a mission to create fresh, original music born of her Brazilian upbringing and passion for jazz. She blends the ever-present samba of her native Brazil with jazz, blues, and songs from around the globe, inspiring the iconic San Francisco Chronicle critic Phil Elwood to enthuse, "Villela doesn't just sing – she actually dances with her voice on top of Brazilian beats." Villela will be joined on this concert date by Brazilian jazz-guitarist Romero Lubambo. Lubambo has an extensive and collaborative career. ev_5ef1ec6dd16e.description: Roopa Mahadevan, vocals; Erika Oba, piano; Chris Trinidad, bass; Keven Amos, drums "exploring diaspora through music" Featuring some of the busiest jazz and crossover musicians on the Bay Area scene, ATOM Ensemble is an exciting new project formed in 2025 over a series of residencies produced by Wyldflowr Arts/Rootstock Arts in Oakland. Vocalist Roopa Mahadevan, pianist and flautist Erika Oba, bassist Chris Trinidad, and drummer Kevin Amos integrate their multifaceted musical and cultural heritages to create a new diasporic sound that is uniquely Bay Area. Their multilingual repertoire features original music drawing on experimental jazz, Indian Carnatic traditions, Japanese folk music, Gregorian Chant, Original Pilipino Music (OPM) and more. Their work has been supported by Oaktown Jazz and the Zellerbach Family Foundation and their debut album releases in Fall 2026. $20 cover charge; byob Students $10 For a reservation, call the bookshop at 415-586-3733

ev_60745e16f19c.description: Tyreek McDole is a multi-award-winning Haitian-American vocalist from Central Florida whose soulful baritone and deeply reflective artistry are making waves across. Rooted in the belief that music is one of the highest forms of communication, McDole approaches performance as a space for healing, reflection, and collective dreaming – treating each concert as both offering and ritual. He first gained national recognition at the 2018 Essentially Ellington Competition at Jazz at Lincoln Center, where he received the Outstanding Vocalist Award, followed by winning first place at the prestigious Sarah Vaughan International Jazz Vocal Competition in 2023. McDole's critically acclaimed debut album, Open Up Your Senses, blends originals with freedom songs, spirituals, and works that speak to justice, unity, and ancestral memory. His sophomore album CHROMA is a continuation of his musical, intellectual and emotional story. Doctorow, Ramon is offered a promotion and cash which could pay for grad school – if he agrees to enter a green-card marriage with his boss's niece. When he agrees, he gets more than he bargained for. "Smoke and Shadows" by Tatyana Tolstaya centers on a Russian professor living in the U.S., navigating her professional life, her intimate relationships, and the mysteries of culture. Told with Tolstaya's sharp, restrained wit, the story zeros in on the experience of living in a new culture, and the confusions and imbalance that can cause. What does it mean to assimilate? These two writers offer two very different perspectives. ev_68f1d1671bae.description: FALL MAIN STAGE 2026 | Tickets on Sale NOV 2026 | NO LATE SEATING Written By Thornton Wilder| Directed by Guest Artist Jeffrey Lo A Stage Manager enters before us calling for time. But it's not a rehearsal they are calling us in for, it's real life. In Thornton Wilder's masterwork Our Town we experience life in three acts: "Daily Life," "Love and Marriage" and finally, "Death and Eternity." In a world where the possibility of humanity losing its grasp on reality looms large, the resonance of this classic reverberates today as strongly as it did when first written and in one of those most stunning scenes in the American cannon, we come face to face with what it is we have already lost. Hailed by Edward Albee as "the greatest American play ever written," this enduring story continues to ask us—generations later—how to use our time, how to love our time and how to run out of time.

ev_6918ea39b538.description: Born in Mexico City and currently based out of New York City, Magos Herrera is a dazzling singer-songwriter, producer, and educator declared as "One of the greatest contemporary interpreters of song" by The Latin Jazz Networ k. With a sultry voice and an unparalleled presence in the contemporary Latin American jazz scene, she is best known for her eloquent vocal improvisation and her singular bold style, which embraces elements of contemporary jazz with Ibero-American melodies and rhythms in a style that elegantly blends and surpasses language boundaries. "She gets way under the skin of the song, recalling great communicators like Edith Piaf or Billie Holiday" is how NPR describes Herrera, who has recorded nine albums. Listed by Forbes Magazine as one of the most creative Mexican artists in the world, Herrera has garnered numerous awards and recognitions, and has received Berklee College of Music's 'Master of Latin Music' award. ev_6961630b7ee2.description: Sevdah is a richly evocative Bosnian word, meaning pining or a longing that is both joyous and painful. It is comparable to Portuguese fado, Greek rembetika or French chanson in its dramatic narratives. Sevdalinka originated during the Ottoman period in Bosnia and Herzegovina and was influenced by the music of the Sephardic Jewish and Roma communities, as well as the music of the Ottoman Empire. Born to a family of bards, Damir Imamovic's immersion in the world of Balkan music was, perhaps, inevitable given that his grandfather Zaim was one of the most recognizable folk musicians and sevdalinka musicians of the mid-20th century. Damir has dedicated his career to performing the music of his homeland and sharing its rich, enchanting melodies and stories with audiences worldwide and educating listeners on its vibrant history. His work has received praise from Pitchfork , The Fader , and the Los Angeles Times . As a film composer, Kirby scored the soundtrack for Cryptozoo , which received the NEXT Innovator Award at Sundance. He scored The Luckiest Man in America starring Paul Walter Hauser and Walton Goggins. Most recently, his music provided the soundtrack to the Oscar-nominated short film Retirement Plan. ev_69d78de9a386.description: Kim Shuck conducts the twice-monthly Virtual Poets series, with featured readers followed by an open mic on the 2nd Monday of each month and an all-open mic session on the 4th Monday of each month. Kim embraces the fool and jester qualities of being a modern poet and artist. She is a devotee of San Francisco, whose hills she wanders nearly always on foot. Her maternal grandparents met at the Polish Hall on Shotwell and she spent many hours with her mother and grandmother wandering the Mission St. Miracle Mile, taking books out of the Mission Branch library and watching aquarium fish on the ground floor of what used to be Hale's. She firmly believes in carrying a bubble wand, keys, pen and notebook and cats cradle string at all times. Kim, whose poetry draws on her multiethnic background which includes Polish and Cherokee heritage, and her experiences as a lifelong resident of San Francisco, served as San Francisco's seventh Poet Laureate, from 2017-2021. As described in Bluegrass Unlimited: "Chords in unexpected places, out of this world harmonies, and some of the most powerfully-arranged material I've ever encountered." RSVP to the Facebook event: Ragamenco A Musical Journey from India to Spain For ten years, RagaMenco has explored the musical pathways connecting India and Spain, bringing together the improvisational traditions of Indian raga with the passion and rhythmic vitality of flamenco and jazz. What began as a meeting of musical cultures has grown into a distinctive language of its own, shaped by a decade of collaboration among Bay Area musicians. Join RagaMenco at the Red Poppy for an evening of ancient traditions, spontaneous conversation, and music continually being reinvented in California. Featuring: Chris Bastian – double bass Mallar Bhattacharya – sarode Nilan Chaudhuri – tabla Javier Jiménez – guitar Luis Jiménez – cajón Satish Pillai – piano Devi SenGupta – vocals Saturday, November 21, 2026 Time: 6:30 pm doors, 7:00 pm – 8:15 pm show Admission: (Online) $25 Students & Seniors – $29 Early Bird – $35 General / $40 Door ABOUT THE ARTISTS: Ragamenco is a Bay Area ensemble of Spanish, Indian, and American musicians exploring connections among North Indian classical music, flamenco, Jazz

ev_6fce8652c613.description: Born in Oakland, California in 1950, Susan Muscarella began playing the piano when she was eight years old. Predisposed to improvising, she was encouraged by her first teacher to play the music she loved – jazz. Muscarella made the decision to become a professional musician while still in high school. In 1975, she was a composition major at UC Berkeley when UC Jazz Ensembles invited her to join its program's faculty. The extracurricular program's students inspired Muscarella to expand the curriculum into a bona fide program of study. She was promoted to Director in 1984, and, for the next five years, grew the program's enrollment, expanded its curriculum and produced the largest annual collegiate jazz festival in the country – the Pacific Coast Collegiate Jazz Festival. The Piano Trios of Bud Powell, Bill Evans & Keith Jarrett will explore the artistry and unique qualities of some of jazz's most beloved piano trios. Can't make it in-person? You can stream it! Click here to register.

ev_70980855fa78.description: FALL MAIN STAGE 2026 | Tickets on Sale NOV 2026 | NO LATE SEATING Written By Thornton Wilder| Directed by Guest Artist Jeffrey Lo A Stage Manager enters before us calling for time. But it's not a rehearsal they are calling us in for, it's real life. In Thornton Wilder's masterwork Our Town we experience life in three acts: "Daily Life," "Love and Marriage" and finally, "Death and Eternity." In a world where the possibility of humanity losing its grasp on reality looms large, the resonance of this classic reverberates today as strongly as it did when first written and in one of those most stunning scenes in the American cannon, we come face to face with what it is we have already lost. Hailed by Edward Albee as "the greatest American play ever written," this enduring story continues to ask us—generations later—how to use our time, how to love our time and how to run out of time.

ev_73a75144413f.description: Don't miss this opportunity to learn tools and tips from one of the most acclaimed bassists in contemporary jazz. Born in Malaysia, raised in Western Australia, and now living in New York City, Linda May Han Oh began playing piano, bassoon, and electric bass before starting upright bass in 2002 at the W.A Academy of Performing Arts (WAAPA), where she graduated with first-class honors. Oh was a James Morrison Scholarship Finalist in 2003, an IAJE Sister in Jazz in 2004, and received the ASCAP Young Jazz Composer's award in 2008. She also received an honorary mention at the 2009 Thelonious Monk Bass Competition. After completing her Masters at the Manhattan School of Music in 2008, she now teaches the pre-college division there, and conducts jazz video conference master classes for high schools around the United States. Can't make it in-person? You can stream it! Click here to register.

Described as "playful", "ebullient", "curious" and "tense", they tear up the rule book and head out into unknown territory. Fred Frith -a composer and improviser best known for the reinvention of the electric guitar that began 50 years ago-returns here to other instruments in his repertoire, namely electric bass (as heard in Art Bears, the Residents, Naked City, French, Frith, Kaiser, Thompson, and countless film sound tracks), and viola, an instrument he's scarcely played since Robert Wyatt's Rock Bottom! Fred has composed a whole collection of new songs for this band which showcase the extraordinary talents of Jordan Glenn, Marié Abe and Kasey Knudsen (whose solos were described by one critic as "towering and arena-worthy!") Born in Tokyo, Japan, Marié Abe

ev_7486dfdc8651.description: Join GRAMMY-winning drummer and educator Ulysses Owens, Jr. for an immersive masterclass: The Art of Understanding Jazz Drumming . In this session, Owens will break down the evolution of jazz drumming into four essential stages: the foundational groove of New Orleans drumming, the driving clarity of swing and bebop as a timekeeping instrument, the shift toward deep musicality as the core foundation for the band, and the cultivation of individuality in style and personal influence. Whether you are looking to unlock your creative voice or sharpen your technical edge, this class will provide actionable insights to immediately increase your understanding and aptitude on the kit. Can't make it in-person? You can stream it! Click here to register.

ev_77d61cd5629a.description: Dedicated to BRAZILIAN music by women composers, Som Dela ("her sound" in Portuguese) is a new quartet composed of four outstanding Bay Area musicians: Jane Lenoir, flute; Irene Sazer, violin; Rebecca Hass, piano; and Michaelle Goerlitz, percussion. All virtuosic and eclectic musicians and composers in Brazilian music and other improvised styles, they have forged well-earned careers in many diverse groups they have performed with, including Berkeley Choro Ensemble, Real Vocal String Quartet, Modern Spark Trio, SF Opera, Ballet and Symphony, VNote Ensemble, Grupo Falso Baiano, Samba Rio, Montclair Women's Big Band and more. The ensemble is dedicated to performing music by women composers from Brazil, including their original compositions, as well as the music of Léa Freire, Luisa Mitre, Carol Panesi, Chiquinha Gonzaga, Anat Cohen, Daniella Spielmann, Lucianna Rabello, and more.

ev_7cadbe1bc61e.description: In 1988, drummer Brian Blade moved to New Orleans to attend Loyola University. It was at this time that he met Jon Cowherd and the roots of the Fellowship Band began. Both Blade and Cowherd were able to study and play with most of the master musicians living in New Orleans, including: John Vidacovich, Ellis Marsalis, Steve Masakowski, Bill Huntington, Mike Pellera, John Mahoney, and Harold Battiste. In 1998, Blade and Cowherd began recording their own music with the group The Fellowship. Together with bandmembers Chris Thomas , Myron Walden , and Melvin Butler , they have performed at esteemed venues like the Village Vanguard and festivals such as the Ottawa Jazz Fest, Newport Jazz Fest, and the New Orleans Jazz Fest. Over their twenty-seven years as a band, they have released seven recordings. Their debut, Fellowship in 1998, Perceptual in 2000, Season of Changes in 2008, Landmarks in 2014, Body And Shadow in 2017, live from the archives in 2022, and Kings Highway in 2023. On this concert date, Brian Blade & The Fellowship Band will feature Blade on drums, Butler on soprano and tenor saxophones, Walden on alto saxophone and bass clarinet, Cowherd on piano, and Thomas on bass. ev_7f49e31be61b.description: Melissa Aldana stands among the defining voices in contemporary jazz. Aldana is a two-time GRAMMY-nominated tenor saxophonist, composer, bandleader, and Blue Note recording artist. The Chilean-born/New York-based artist has earned international recognition for her commanding sound, emotional depth, and singular artistic vision. On stage, Aldana's unmistakable tenor sound moves between extraordinary intimacy and power; bringing together virtuosity, spontaneity, and an emotional immediacy that can completely command a room. With an uncompromising artistic vision, an ever-expanding body of work, and extraordinary creative momentum, Aldana continues to shape the direction of contemporary jazz on the international stage. ev_812e792ae273.description: DINNER SHOW with WRECKLESS STRANGERS Wreckless Strangers is a collective of friends and musicians carrying the torch for San Francisco's grand rock 'n' roll tradition. Their unique blend of "Ameri-Cali Soul" melds the contemporary blues stylings of Bonnie Raitt and Boz Scaggs; the songwriting sensibilities of Sons of Champlin and Fleetwood Mac; the swashbuckling Americana of the Lost Planet Airmen and Peter Rowan; and the funk of Sly Stone and Tower of Power with a dash of Grateful Dead and Jefferson Airplane for flavor and unpredictability. With soaring vocal harmonies and burning instrumental improvisation framed in concise and poignant original songwriting, Wreckless Strangers seek to honor and carry forth the brand of free-spirited musical fun and adventure that defines the Bay Area.

ev_86b8feff18ee.description: Chris Cain offers up a soulful stew of Memphis style electric blues. His powerfully deep vocals and jazz-inspired blues guitar riffs are unforgettable; uniquely his own, while reminiscent of the legendary BB King and Albert King. As a child, Cain attended concerts with his dad to hear many of the great blues artists of the time. When Cain burst onto the blues scene in 1987 with his award-winning debut album, he soon found himself sharing the stage and trading licks with a few of those legends, including Albert King and Albert Collins. Cain has released a dozen albums, each filled with soul-stirring songs pulled from his own blues drenched heart. His brand of blues is unforgettable. Now, with Good Intentions Gone Bad , Cain will find his largest audience yet, as his good musical intentions continue to pay off. According to Kid Andersen, there's no better blues player working today. "Chris Cain is the rarity whose blues prowess is so undeniable that he has gained everyone's approval. Ask any of your favorite guitar players who they think are the greatest living masters of the instrument, chances are they will all have Chris Cain at the very top of their list." Chris Cain Website Spon

ev_8708bef5fffe.description: Freddie Bryant 's latest recording project is his most intimate and his first complete album of solo guitar. Solo Bossa features 14 of his original compositions written over the last four decades. The title refers to bossa nova and many of the tracks have that classic feel made famous in the early 1960's. The music takes the journey from bossa to samba as well as baiao, bolero, waltz and a sultry ballad-bossa in 7/4. Solo Bossa was preceded by Upper West Side Love Story an epic song cycle featuring a nonet fronted by the acclaimed jazz singer, Carla Cook. It's a double CD/90min with sixteen songs with his "passionate lyrics and colorful music." (Carlo Wolff/Downbeat). It was featured in the NY Daily News and Downbeat listed it as "Best CDs of 2023." The all-star cast also includes Regina Carter on violin and saxophonists Donny McCaslin and Steve Wilson along with strings and a stellar rhythm section. Visit the website: https://upperwestsidelovestory.com/ for more info. Freddie received a master's degree in classical guitar from Yale School of Music and is in demand in the New York jazz and Brazilian scenes where he has worked with Eliane Elias, Tom Harrell and many others. ev_8c7d08341fdb.description: Painted in the broadest of strokes, the stories of Alfredo Rodriguez and Pedrito Martinez may seem similar: both started life in Havana, discovered their gifts and passions for music and headed to the United States, where they melded the music of their homeland with a wide variety of influences, each in his own deeply personal way. Rodriguez was born into a musical family, his father a popular singer and TV host. Martinez, on the other hand, honed his craft on the streets of Havana, learning the deeply-rooted percussion and vocal style of Afro-Cuban folkloric and religious music. "What makes this [project] completely different is that I came from the folkloric side and Alfredo came from the classical side. ev_8d7c56b3403a.description: Russia, 1927. Ten years after the Revolution toppled the Romanov family, a rumor lingers among the people that the youngest royal daughter, Anastasia, survived. We follow a young woman named Anya, who remembers almost nothing of her past, as she joins a quick-thinking con man and a former aristocrat on a journey to Paris to convince the Dowager Empress that Anya is her long-lost granddaughter. With a Soviet officer on their trail and fragments of memory beginning to surface, Anya must face a question she never expected: what if the story they have rehearsed is her own? Stanford's vocalists and instrumentalists present Anastasia, the 2016 musical inspired by the beloved 1997 animated film, a story about who we become when the past goes missing. Directed by Ariela Morgenstern, with Musical Director Marie-Louise Catsalis and Vocal Director Benjamin Liupaogo. Book by Terrence McNally Music by Stephen Flaherty Lyrics by Lynn Ahrens Inspired by the Twentieth Century Fox Motion Pictures by special arrangement with Buena Vista Theatrical From the play by Marcelle Maurette as adapted by Guy Bolton Admission Information Tickets on sale soon! His musical directions converge in the genre of Americana, blending Jazz, pop, folk, and classical. A Los Angeles native and award-winning composer, Carlson has also been an accomplished jazz guitarist, producer, music professor and author. Since 2009, he has been resident composer for Jeff Sanford's Cartoon Jazz Orchestra. The Collective's premiere performance at Bird & Beckett on 1/22/27 will feature Kevin Gerzevitz, piano; Michelle Maruyama, violin; Carla Wilson, bassoon and Luke Kirley, tuba/euphonium. Kevin Gerzevitz's compositions and arrangements will also be performed. Carlson's recent discography includes the title and three additional selections on Jeff Sanford's Playland at the Beach CD (2023), available on Spotify and Bandcamp; Down by the Riverside: Theme and Variations CD (2022) on Bandcamp; and Nothing Wrong (2019), a Cartoon Jazz CD comprised entirely of his compositions, on Bandcamp. ev_8f4d8bfa83cf.description: The well-oiled machine that is the road show of two intrepid archive divers, San Francisco's Tate Swindell and Vienna's Thomas Antonic, reaches Tate's home base with a program built around the recording of Allen Ginsberg 1980 Graz, Austria poetry event with Peter Orlofsky and musician Steven Taylor dubbed "America: Give A Shit," now a 2026 double lp release on Swindell's Unrequited Records label, and Antonic's recently published book, The Three Wives of Queer William S. Burroughs (Beatdom, 2026). (L-R) Taylor/Ginsberg/Orlofsky – photo by Saul Shapiro Tate and Thomas have lately been presenting programs focused on the Ginsberg lp in Budapest, Vienna, Prague and Graz. Thomas was last heard at Bird & Beckett in January 2022 presenting his previous book, Amongst Nazis: William S. Burroughs in Vienna 1936/37 . Tate is well known to San Francisco beats, baby beats and post beats for his production of cultural materials — books, lps, readings, concerts — derived from his archive explorations and personal contacts with the likes of Harold Norse, Gregory Corso, Neeli Cherkovski and countless others through the past couple of decades.

Along the way he studied classical music, jazz, played in basements and coliseums and absorbed the Bay Area Multi Kulti , the funk of New Orleans, and the New York Downtown edge. ev_922d62c3bff8.description: With a career spanning more than twenty years and six studio albums, Las Migas have become one of the most internationally acclaimed Spanish bands. They have performed in more than fifty countries and have been nominated four times for the Latin GRAMMY Award in the Best Flamenco Album category (2016, 2022, 2024, and 2025), winning the award twice. They have also received the prestigious MIN Award in 2019 and 2023 for their albums Rumberas and Libres , respectively. In the spring of 2025, Las Migas released Flamencas , a tribute to the essence and purity of flamenco. In this work, the band evolves its sound toward a more contemporary expression, wrapped in a powerful visual identity showcased in the video for "Celos," directed by renowned fashion photographer Javier Biosca. The recording won the Latin GRAMMY Award for Best Flamenco Album. Throughout their career, Las Migas have collaborated with a wide array of acclaimed artists such as Estrella Morente, Viva Suecia, Rozalén, El Kanka, Kevin Johansen, Tomatito, Josemi Carmona, and Loli Molina. YOYOKA is a San Francisco Bay Area-based jazz fusion ensemble blending Japanese and American jazz fusion traditions with modern improvisation and vibrant rhythmic interplay. Led by bassist and composer Ken Okada , the group features GRAMMY award-winning saxophonist Ben Torres , DownBeat 'Rising Star' guitarist Hristo Vitchev , four-time GRAMMY award nominee Murray Low , and internationally acclaimed teenage drumming prodigy YOYOKA , known for her groove, musical depth, and commanding stage presence. The band has become a fixture of the Bay Area jazz scene, consistently selling out premier venues. Their international profile continues to grow, highlighted by a successful 2025 European tour, featuring sold-out performances at Barcelona's historic Jamboree and a headlining appearance at Bulgaria's Bansko International Jazz Festival. She began to develop her style as a jazz singer while studying with Merrill Hoover, a well known jazz pianist best known for his eloquent accompaniment of vocalists such as Ernestine Anderson, Anita O'Day, and Mary Stallings. This rare opportunity set the foundation for her to establish her own unique approach to singing as she fell in love with the jazz standard. Known for her command of the lyric, beautiful soothing tone, soulful improvisation, and carefully chosen repertoire, Dima keeps alive the true art of the jazz singer. She's backed on this date by the best in the business, attesting to the respect she merits for her art.

The repertoire is straight-up traditional bluegrass, although the occasional old-time or folk-inflected choice will pop up. The format is the old-fashioned song circle, with each participant getting a turn to call a song and set its key, pace, and feel. An experienced jam leader and bass player are always present to help keep things on track. Everyone is welcome — come on down!

ev_9b863080c835.description: Andy McKee is one of the world's finest acoustic guitarists; evident from the accolades he's received throughout his career. It's his youthful energy, attention to song structure, and melodic content that elevates him to a peerless level. McKee entertains both the eye and the ear as he magically transforms the steel string guitar into a full orchestra via his use of altered tunings, tapping, partial capos, percussive hits, and a signature two-handed fretting technique. McKee's crossover success has helped him to achieve millions upon millions of YouTube viewers, underscoring his emergence as one of today's most unique and influential artists. His song "Drifting" became one of the first YouTube viral videos, logging nearly 60 million views. He also curates his own annual guitar retreat called Musicarium . McKee's tour dates have taken him through Europe, Asia, Australia, and North America, including tours with legendary artists ranging from Dream Theater to Tommy Emmanuel. ev_9ccb471abf5e.description: Sunny Jain is a composer, drummer, dhol player and thought leader. While growing up with a deep cultural connection to his South Asian heritage, Jain also fell in love with jazz music and prog rock. He has been at the zeitgeist of America's South Asian sounds for the past two decades. He founded and plays dhol in the pioneering Brooklyn band, Red Baraat, and has drummed with some of the top South Asian artists on the scene today. Sunny Jain's Wild Wild East band encompasses myriad facets of Jain's identity, and sonically paints the journey of his own family's immigration story. He sources musical inspiration from the scores of Bollywood classics, Punjabi folk traditions, jazz improvisation, and rollicking psychedelic styles. "The indefatigable drummer and dhol player Sunny Jain is an unrepentant maximalist. Think of a genre, and it's probably somewhere in his compositions, yet the musician's hullabaloo stands on considered conceptual ground." – The New Yorker Sunny Jain Website (Ticket Includes 5% City of Santa Cruz Admission Tax) .embed-container { position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden; max-width: 100%; } .embed-container iframe, .embed-container

Cantor Arts Center presents Forms & Frequencies, a Thursday night music series featuring musicians and sound artists from the Bay Area and beyond. Join us on Thursday, December 3 for a night of pounding electronics and unruly physicality with Xina Xurner and Tzotzona, with visuals by artist Christopher Richmond. Xina Xurner is a Los Angeles-based sadical and sexperimental music and performance duo with vocalist, sculptor, and performance artist Young Joon Kwak and musician and producer Marvin Astorga. Fusing industrial noise, power electronics, dark club-wrecking beats, electric guitar, and extreme vocal distortion, their body-shaking live shows unleash queer trans-femme rage, refusal, and joy. Creating an atmosphere that feels part club, part collective exorcism, Xina Xurner's performance will be paired with visuals by artist Christopher Richmond, whose alien and terrestrial landscapes juxtapose reality and illusion, using handmade props, special photography, and varied drawing styles to present multiple pictorial universes in constant kinetic interaction. He's spent two decades leading the DownBeat Critics and Readers polls and has won fifteen Jazz Journalists Association Awards for "Male Vocalist of the Year." Pianist and two-time GRAMMY nominee Sands is an emerging jazz force. His abundant piano technique perfectly matches his ambition, accomplishing a much deeper musical goal: a fresh look at the entire spectrum of jazz. A protégé of Dr. Billy Taylor, Sands released his debut album at the age of twelve. He came to wider prominence through his work as a member of two bands led by iconic bassist Christian McBride: the Christian McBride Trio and Inside Straight. ev_a28d401eddbc.description: Sevdah is a richly evocative Bosnian word, meaning pining or a longing that is both joyous and painful. It is comparable to Portuguese fado, Greek rembetika or French chanson in its dramatic narratives. Sevdalinka originated during the Ottoman period in Bosnia and Herzegovina and was influenced by the music of the Sephardic Jewish and Roma communities, as well as the music of the Ottoman Empire. Born to a family of bards, Damir Imamovic's immersion in the world of Balkan music was, perhaps, inevitable given that his grandfather Zaim was one of the most recognizable folk musicians and sevdalinka musicians of the mid-20th century. Damir has dedicated his career to performing the music of his homeland and sharing its rich, enchanting melodies and stories with audiences worldwide and educating listeners on its vibrant history. Beyond the stage, she contributes her talents to influential arts organizations such as The National Jazz Museum in Harlem, Jazz Houston, and The Woodshed Network. As one of Jazz at Lincoln Center's latest rising stars, Nkwelle is poised to shape the future of jazz. ev_a41ad1380305.description: Born in Malaysia, raised in Western Australia, and now living in New York City, Linda May Han Oh began playing piano, bassoon, and electric bass before starting upright bass in 2002 at the W.A Academy of Performing Arts (WAAPA), where she graduated with first-class honors. Oh was a James Morrison Scholarship Finalist in 2003, an IAJE Sister in Jazz in 2004, and received the ASCAP Young Jazz Composer's award in 2008. She also received an honorary mention at the 2009 Thelonious Monk Bass Competition. After completing her Masters at the Manhattan School of Music in 2008, she now teaches the pre-college division there, and conducts jazz video conference master classes for high schools around the United States. Oh has performed with the likes of Joe Lovano, Steve Wilson, Vijay Iyer, Dave Douglas, Kenny Barron, Geri Allen, Fabian Almazan, Terri Lyne Carrington, and is currently the bassist for Pat Metheny. ev_a6a480508d3b.description: The Arun Ramamurthy Trio creates a groundbreaking fusion of South Indian Carnatic traditions with contemporary jazz, weaving masterful improvisations through ancient ragas and modern rhythms. Brooklyn violinist Arun Ramamurthy is a self-described Indo-jazz explorer who creates strikingly beautiful music fusing the spirit of raga music and jazz. Steeped in the Carnatic musical tradition of South India, but also versed in North Indian Hindustani forms, he's a prolific composer who has created scores for plays, dance productions, and other fellow musicians. His powerhouse trio features electric bassist Damon Banks , a global force also versed in West and North African rhythms, and drummer Sameer Gupta . This unique ensemble has performed on many prestigious stages, including Jazz at Lincoln Center, The Kennedy Center, Northampton Jazz Festival, Yerba Buena Gardens and Amsterdam's Bimhuis. The band's latest release, New Moon , shines a light on the teachings and wisdom of our ancestors, and the lessons we take on our own personal journeys. ev_ab66cd9adcf3.description: The Garage Jam is an open, friendly bluegrass circle that meets the first and third Monday of every month, from 6 to 8 pm. All kinds of pickers show up, from rank beginners to grizzled veterans, plus folks who just come to listen and socialize. The repertoire is straight-up traditional bluegrass, although the occasional old-time or folk-inflected choice will pop up. The format is the old-fashioned song circle, with each participant getting a turn to call a song and set its key, pace, and feel. An experienced jam leader and bass player are always present to help keep things on track. Everyone is welcome — come on down!

ev_b2d5f11d26b9.description: Camila Meza is a groundbreaking artist, celebrated as a guitarist, vocalist, and composer. With a signature sound that combines jazz with Latin American folklore and poetic songwriting, Meza has captivated audiences worldwide. The New York Times emphasizes her dual talent as a profound guitarist and a compelling singer. Her artistry, described as an "appealing combination of lightness and depth" showcases her clear, expressive voice and sophisticated guitar playing – whether in intricate self-accompaniment or dazzling solos. As a bandleader, she has released five acclaimed albums, with Traces (2016) earning two Independent Music Awards and Ámbar (2019) winning Chile's prestigious Pulsar Prize and receiving a Dutch Edison Awards nomination. Her performances have graced iconic stages such as Carnegie Hall and The Kennedy Center, and she has appeared on NPR's Tiny Desk Concert and Jazz Night in America . In 2025, Meza released her highly anticipated album Portal on Ground Up Music Label. Co-produced by pianist Shai Maestro, this project marked a new chapter in her career, featuring all-original compositions that further showcase her depth as an artist. Presented by Opera Parallèle Doors open at 5:30PM Workshop starts at 6:00PM Learn the basics of Gullah Stick Pounding in this free workshop led by Melanie DeMore. We will create a foot stomping, hand-clapping rhythmic community and combine it with singing spirituals and songs of protest and peace. Participants will learn about Gullah/Geechee culture through its dynamic music and rhythmic heart. We will, as a community, turn the whole place into a living, breathing drum. About Melanie DeMore Melanie DeMore is a three-time Grammy-nominated singer, composer, choral conductor, and vocal activist who believes in the power of voices raised together. A sought-after workshop leader and music director, she has led choirs and community groups across North America and beyond. A founding member of the Grammy-nominated Linda Tillery and the Cultural Heritage Choir, DeMore uses music as a tool for healing, connection, and social change, believing that "a song can hold you up when there seems to be no ground beneath you." Polzak performs rockabilly and 60's country music with the religious fervor of Jerry Lee Lewis and Johnny Cash and delivers a Honky Tonk ballad with the sincerity of Merle Haggard and Waylon Jennings. Mitch will bring a room to a fevered pitch of joyous energy on the dance floor and then tell you a story in a song like two old friends sitting at a kitchen table at midnight.

ev_b77dedc49690.description: Held on 2nd Saturdays,12-3pm, at 1005 Railroad Ave, in Santa Clara, CA. The Santa Clara Historic Train Depot, Bluegrass, Country, Old Time, & Folk jam is free and open to intermediate and experienced stringed instrument players. The jam started in 2012, and is now on its 11th year. The The South Bay Historic Railroad Society kindly lends chairs and space for the jam. The jam takes place on the patio on sunny days in front of the historic depot and train museum. When the weather is inclement, the jam moves into the train museum. Parking is free in front of the depot museum, $5.50 if you park in the caltran parking lot.
ev_b77dedc49690.title: Santa Clara Bluegrass Train Jam

ev_b9cabeeeb185.description: FALL MAIN STAGE 2026 | Tickets on Sale NOV 2026 | NO LATE SEATING Written By Thornton Wilder| Directed by Guest Artist Jeffrey Lo A Stage Manager enters before us calling for time. But it's not a rehearsal they are calling us in for, it's real life. In Thornton Wilder's masterwork Our Town we experience life in three acts: "Daily Life," "Love and Marriage" and finally, "Death and Eternity." In a world where the possibility of humanity losing its grasp on reality looms large, the resonance of this classic reverberates today as strongly as it did when first written and in one of those most stunning scenes in the American cannon, we come face to face with what it is we have already lost. Hailed by Edward Albee as "the greatest American play ever written," this enduring story continues to ask us—generations later—how to use our time, how to love our time and how to run out of time.

After a name change and a self-released 10-inch album called Sneakers, which sold amazingly well, the band caught the attention of Columbia Records, who signed them and released their first real album, Supersnazz, on the Epic label. Their next two albums were released on the Kama Sutra label: Flamingo, and the now revered classic Teenage Head. Lead singer Roy Loney then left the band and lead guitarist Cyril Jordan moved the group to England, with Chris Wilson (formerly of Loose Gravel) taking over as front man. They continued their style of straight-ahead guitar-driven rock n' roll but this time with a more 60's rather than 50's influence.
