Strom has played alongside many well-known artists, including Manhattan Transfer, Gladys Knight, Natalie Cole, and more. In addition to her solo albums, Intention , Sojourn and Moving Day: The Music of John Shifflett, she has recorded on more than forty albums with various jazz and pop artists. She is an endorsing artist and clinician for Selmer saxophones. ev_bd3369ed65e6.description: Isaiah Sharkey stands at the confluence of modern soul, jazz, R&B, and Black American guitar tradition, carrying forward a lineage that links George Benson, Curtis Mayfield, Wes Montgomery, and Jimi Hendrix, while forging a vocabulary entirely his own. A GRAMMY award-winning guitarist, vocalist, composer, and producer, Sharkey has become one of the most respected musicians of his generation – celebrated for his sophisticated harmonic sensibility, unmistakable tone, and ability to shape-shift effortlessly between musical worlds. Sharkey's guitar work on D'Angelo's landmark album Black Messiah earned him a GRAMMY Award and a position among the most innovative guitarists shaping contemporary Black music. As a solo artist, Sharkey has developed a distinctive, emotionally resonant sound that blends deep-pocket groove, virtuosic improvisation, and songwriter-driven storytelling. His latest album, RED , introduced audiences to his modern fusion of soul, R&B, jazz, and guitar-based narrative. His follow-up projects – each expanding his sonic palette – solidify his standing as an artist capable of speaking fluently to instrumental purists and mainstream audiences alike. ev_bde6224542f2.description: Throughout his career, trumpeter Ambrose Akinmusire has paradoxically situated himself in both the center and the periphery of jazz, and has also emerged in classical and hip hop circles. He's on a perpetual quest for new paradigms, masterfully weaving inspiration from other genres, arts, and life into compositions that are as poetic and graceful as they are bold and unflinching. His unorthodox approach to sound and composition make him a regular on critics polls and have earned him numerous grants and commissions. Born and raised in Oakland, California, Akinmusire (pronounced ah-kin-MOO-sir-ee) was a member of the Berkeley High School Jazz Ensemble when he caught the attention of saxophonist Steve Coleman. Akinmusire was asked to join Coleman's Five Elements, embarking on a European tour when he was just a nineteen-year-old student at the Manhattan School of Music. After returning to the West Coast to pursue a master's degree at the University of Southern California, Akinmusire went on to attend the Thelonious Monk Institute of Jazz in Los Angeles, where he studied with Herbie Hancock, Wayne Shorter and Terence Blanchard. ev_bf4f9126eb88.description: Jason Crosby and friends bring the music of Vince Guaraldi and The Grateful Dead to Kuumbwa. After decades on the road as one of rock's most in-demand sidemen touring with the likes of Susan Tedeschi, Robert Randolph and others, multi-instrumentalist Jason Crosby took time for himself. The result was his 2017 solo album, Cryptologic , and a relationship with Nashville's Blue Rose label. The album revealed the keyboard/violin/guitar player to be an honest, thoughtful lyricist and songwriter in his own right, singing and playing all the instruments on half of the tracks and bringing in Northern California stalwarts The Mother Hips for the rest of it. It was also inspired by the longtime New Yorker's earlier move to the Bay Area of California, where he found a kindred musical community that included The Mother Hips and the Grateful Dead's Phil Lesh and Bob Weir. ev_c0fbd41076a8.description: Joshua Redman acknowledges that the title of his new Blue Note album, Words Fall Short , could be viewed ironically. His previous and widely acclaimed Where Are We was his first to pair a vocalist with one of his many monumental quartets; yet Words Fall Short is anything but a comment on the saxophonist's last triumph. More accurately, his latest offering is an organic next step, a collection of previously unheard originals brought to life by inspiring new collaborators. "It's impossible for me to will a project into being," he says of the wide-ranging adventures he has embarked upon in what is now his fourth decade as a recording artist. "This album came out of a working environment that inspired me to dig into compositions that hadn't found a home yet." For Redman, the shifting moods of wistfulness, aspiration, sadness and resolve contained in Words Fall Short signify his embrace of what he describes as "the beauty of human imperfection. We follow a young woman named Anya, who remembers almost nothing of her past, as she joins a quick-thinking con man and a former aristocrat on a journey to Paris to convince the Dowager Empress that Anya is her long-lost granddaughter. With a Soviet officer on their trail and fragments of memory beginning to surface, Anya must face a question she never expected: what if the story they have rehearsed is her own? Stanford's vocalists and instrumentalists present Anastasia, the 2016 musical inspired by the beloved 1997 animated film, a story about who we become when the past goes missing. Directed by Ariela Morgenstern, with Musical Director Marie-Louise Catsalis and Vocal Director Benjamin Liupaogo. Book by Terrence McNally Music by Stephen Flaherty Lyrics by Lynn Ahrens Inspired by the Twentieth Century Fox Motion Pictures by special arrangement with Buena Vista Theatrical From the play by Marcelle Maurette as adapted by Guy Bolton Admission Information Tickets on sale soon! Her latest album, Anohin , a duo with pianist Marta Sanchez, was released in March 2024; and during its release tour Grtand was deemed "excellent on the tenor horn" and "an unpretentious and incredibly soulful singer" by JazzWise. ev_cad39d55754e.description: On May 11, 1987, pianist Michel Petrucciani , bassist Dave Holland , and drummer Eliot Zigmund took the Kuumbwa stage for a remarkable concert – a special stop on the trio's only tour – which featured these three giants of modern jazz in peak creative form. Petrucciani passed away in 1999, but his legacy shines in the new lovingly-restored release of this historic night. The never-before-released recording, titled Kuumbwa is available now from Elemental Music in deluxe edition as a 2-LP 180-gram vinyl set, with a sixteen-page booklet of liner notes and rare photos. We will celebrate the release of this Petrucciani masterstroke with 'Kuumbwa' – The Story Behind the Album , featuring a conversation between Kuumbwa Co-Founder Tim Jackson, and the album's producer Zev Feldman. You'll hear about the concert itself, the rediscovery and preparation of the tapes, the release production, as well as hear samples of the album. Can't make it in-person? You can stream it! Click here to register.

ev_cb04f7e8892e.description: In celebration of the centennial of trumpeter Miles Davis, the Marcus Shelby Nonet presents Birth of the Cool: Revisited , featuring music from the groundbreaking Davis recording performed in its original instrumentation. Birth of the Cool was not a singular session, but the composite work of a young innovative genius at the beginning of a long and storied career; surrounded and supported by a group of forward thinking musicians, composers, and arrangers. Birth of the Cool remains one of the most enduring recordings in the history of music – let alone jazz. The Marcus Shelby Nonet consists of nine San Francisco Bay Area master musicians, all of whom are a part of the Marcus Shelby New Orchestra: Heidi Tretheren on French horn, Remee Ashley on trombone, Mike Olmos on trumpet, Tony Peebles on alto saxophone, Melecio Magdaluyo on baritone saxophone, Jonathan Seiberlich on tuba, Greg Jacobs on piano, Shelby on bass, and Jemal Ramirez on drums. Born in Lahore, Pakistan, Sukhawat is a versatile singer based out of the San Francisco Bay Area and has performed internationally in a career spanning nearly 50 years. In addition to presenting North Indian and Pakistani traditional music, he has recorded and performed extensively with several world fusion music ensembles. This concert will feature presentations of classical and light classical forms including qawwali, ghazal, khayal, thumrl and sufiana kalam. ev_ce4b1740fcf1.description: Leaving Dublin, Ireland where he was born and raised until the age of 22, David Nihill got drunk on travel and never quite hit sobriety of it. He has lived and worked in twelve countries and visited over seventy. His shows draw on his wide travels, cultural observations, attempts at language study, (occasional) international drinking session(s) and being a mildly confused immigrant. His latest show Taking Tangents promised to do just that :) David is the winner of the prestigious annual San Francisco Comedy Competition, (previous finalists include Robin Williams, Ellen DeGeneres and Dana Carvey) and runner-up in the Moth's largest US Grandslam storytelling competition. Also a bestselling writer, David recorded his debut special for Dry Bar Comedy in 2019, his follow ups Cultural Appreciation in 2023 and Shelf Help in 2025, and has been featured on TED.com, Sirius XM, Just For Laughs, Netflix if a Joke Fest, The Late Late Show, The Irish Independent, Inc, NPR, and the Huffington Post among others. A festival favorite, David's videos have also gone viral many times over with over 1 billion views and a social following of over 2 million people. David Nihill Website info/tickets/questi

Sima Bina is a renowned Iranian folk singer, songwriter, and researcher. She is celebrated for her contributions to preserving and promoting Persian folk music and culture. Sima Bina was born in 1945, in Khorasan, Iran. Her passion for folk music emerged from her childhood experiences, as she grew up surrounded by traditional Persian melodies and rhythms. She began singing at an early age and was particularly drawn to the rich tapestry of regional folk songs from different parts of Iran. Her professional career grew in the 1960s when she started performing publicly and recording albums. Bina's distinctive voice and her ability to interpret traditional songs with authenticity quickly earned her recognition within Iran and abroad. Bina is also a dedicated researcher and educator. Throughout her career, Bina has tirelessly worked to collect, document, and preserve Persian folk music, traveling to remote regions of Iran to learn from local musicians and record their songs. ev_d17048e46f0c.description: The Wooten Brothers ' first public performance occurred in Hawaii in 1966 and established their identity as prodigies. Since then, Victor Wooten and the Wooten Brothers (brothers Regi, Roy , and Joseph ) have racked up ten GRAMMY wins, and twenty-six nominations. The youngest of the family, Victor, the brother who learned from all his older brothers, has been named one of the ten greatest bass players of all time by Rolling Stone Magazine . As a family band, they are second to none. The Brothers' music bends and defines genres; amplifies centuries, and spans continents. The Wooten Brothers began playing R&B before expanding to jazz, jazz fusion, classical, and country. They emerged in 1985 on Arista Records with their release, The Wootens , combining electronic music, funk, soul, disco, and boogie – offering only a sliver of the Wooten whole. The Wooten whole is all of that...and classical, and jazz, and country, and rock-and-roll. Connecting a musically deep past to a musical future, The Wooten Brothers build bridges across genres. In 1983, Raymond Carver responded to Cheever's story, answering the question "And then what?" and adding some questions of his own. A bustling city center not unlike Times Square in the 70's filled with sin and sex is the backdrop where gangs, street preachers, sex addicts, pimps, prostitutes and pornographers live and work. People of this world describe the time period of these songs as the Raw Wave. A wave of new analog technology that hit the city wiping away many of the mores and pretense of the past. ev_d653043fd3cb.description: Born in Norman, Oklahoma in 1985, Champian Fulton was recognized by The Detroit Free Press as the "most gifted pure Jazz singer of her generation." A pianist and vocalist with a career spanning more than twenty years, Fulton has released twenty albums as a bandleader and has performed in more than twenty-five countries. She has been recognized with numerous awards, including 'Album of the Year' in the NYC Jazz Record (2018, 2020, 2023) and 'Pianist' and 'Vocalist of the Year' by Hot House Magazine . She regularly appears in both the Jazz Journalist Awards and DownBeat's 'Rising Star' Critics Poll. An unforgettable performer, "Every song is a work of art in Champian's hands and voice" according to The Absolute Sound . Her "galvanizing presence" ( The New Yorker ) and her alluring musical presentation have made her, as The New York Times writes, "a charming young steward of the mainstream jazz tradition." ev_da02dd1e1410.description: Benny Green was born in New York City in 1963 and grew up in Berkeley, California. His father, who played the tenor saxophone, introduced him to jazz at an early age through his record collection that included Thelonious Monk, Charlie Parker, Billie Holiday, Ray Charles, and many founding voices of the genre. He began piano lessons at the age of seven, with his first paid performance at twelve. His major concert stage debut was in 1978 at the Monterey Jazz Festival as a member of the MJF High School All-Stars (now known as the Next Generation Jazz Orchestra). As a band leader, Green recorded two albums for the Dutch Criss Cross label in the late 1980s before signing to Blue Note Records in 1990. He remained with the label for ten years recording seven albums, as well as two albums for its Japanese subsidiary, Toshiba–EMI. Oscar Peterson named Green as his protegé in 1992, and chose Green as the recipient of the Glenn Gould Award for excellence in Music and Communication. He recorded many albums as a sideman throughout the 1980s and 90s, including a duet with Diana Krall on her GRAMMY Award winning album, All For You . He began studying with pianist Alla Epelbaum at The Calderone School of Music and Bob Mikula from an early age, and soon after enrolled in Jazz House Kids and NJPAC Jazz For Teens. Thompson later was admitted to The Juilliard School where he graduated with both his Bachelor's and Master's of Music degrees, and went on to further his education in Theology and the Arts at Fuller Theological Seminary. Thompson joined the John Pizzarelli Trio in 2019 and has performed with other major artists such as Christian McBride, Steve Turre, Catherine Russell, and Buster Williams. His recording debut was featured on Jazz at Lincoln Center's Handful of Keys album with the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra with Wynton Marsalis, and he has since released multiple recordings as a leader. Anglade's performances are a reflection of her roots: rich in simplicity, an appreciation for the past and finding wonder in ordinary moments. Anglade brings clarity and depth to interpretations shaped by the legendary voices of Sarah Vaughan, Ella Fitzgerald, Shirley Horn, Carmen McRae, Michel Legrand and Barbra Streisand, among others. Her 2022 release Venez Donc Chez Moi earned a Juno nomination, and in 2023 she was awarded the 'Prix Opus' for Jazz Concert of the Year. An international touring artist, Anglade has headlined jazz festivals across the United States, Canada, Mexico, United Kingdom, and Europe, captivating audiences through her innate storytelling. Her conversational style bridges the gap between singer and listener, making each performance intimate and personal. Since 2009, he has been resident composer for Jeff Sanford's Cartoon Jazz Orchestra. The Collective's premiere performance at Bird & Beckett on 1/22/27 will feature Kevin Gerzevitz, piano; Michelle Maruyama, violin; Carla Wilson, bassoon and Luke Kirley, tuba/euphonium. Kevin Gerzevitz's compositions and arrangements will also be performed. ev_e61ea4228006.description: The Klezmatics return with a powerful new album and live program. Celebrating forty years at the forefront of global roots music, the band brings We Were Made For These Times to the stage – a bold, cross-cultural project shaped by songs of protest, resilience, and radical joy. Blending Yiddish song with Black gospel, Latin rhythms, and avant-jazz, The Klezmatics transform tradition into a living, evolving musical language – urgent, joyful, and deeply relevant today. World-renowned and GRAMMY-winning superstars of the klezmer world, The Klezmatics erupted out of New York City's East Village in 1986 and revitalized klezmer for the new century with music that is steeped in Eastern European Jewish tradition and spirituality, while incorporating contemporary themes such as human rights and anti-fundamentalism with eclectic musical influences. They have released thirteen albums of wild, spiritual, provocative, reflective, and ecstatically danceable music, forever redefining and transcending traditional labels. ev_e71e25f84768.description: Hamilton de Holanda is one of Brazil's most celebrated musicians, a global ambassador for Brazilian music, and a master of improvisation. Picking up the mandolin at the age of five, he revolutionized the 10-string version of the instrument, blending Brazilian traditions like choro with jazz and other global influences. A four-time Latin GRAMMY winner with seventeen nominations, de Holanda has earned international recognition and amassed over fourteen million streams across 180 countries, with 800,000 monthly listeners on Spotify in 2024. His music is rooted in family encouragement, a university degree in composition, and the vibrant choro street jams of Brasília. As an educator and cultural advocate, he co-founded the world's first Choro School in Brasília and led the movement to establish a National Day of Choro in Brazil. His collaborations include legends like Wynton Marsalis, Chick Corea, and Milton Nascimento, and he has graced stages at iconic venues and festivals such as Rock in Rio, Montreux, and Newport Jazz. De Holanda's work connects cultures, celebrates diversity, and expands the boundaries of music, solidifying his place as an innovator and educator in the global music

ev_e960cd8cfd07.description: Raga Music on a Sunday morning with the rare, transformative beauty of a live time specific Morning Raga. In the Indian classical tradition, ragas are intimate expressions aligned with specific times of day—a concept known as samay raga . Because most modern concerts take place in the evening, hearing morning ragas performed live during their intended hours is a rarity. When done properly, the music resonates in natural harmony with the surrounding atmosphere, creating a deeply grounding and tranquil experience. Join us at Bird & Beckett Books & Records for our Monthly Morning Raga Series on Dec 27th , featuring Bansuri flutist, Akshay Naresh. Akshay Naresh is based in the San Francisco Bay Area, with more than two decades of devotion to the instrument. He trained in Hindustani classical music under Pandit Prasad Bhandarker and in Carnatic classical music under Shri Shashank, and his playing carries both traditions. He performs light music concerts, has collaborated with artists in the Bay Area, and produces music in his spare time. ev_e9d88d3b2c10.description: For over sixty years, South Africa's five-time GRAMMY award-winners Ladysmith Black Mambazo have warmed the hearts of audiences worldwide with uplifting vocal harmonies, signature dance moves and charming stage presence. It was Paul Simon's 1987 Graceland album that first introduced Ladysmith Black Mambazo to the world; and the late former South African President Nelson Mandela designated the group "South Africa's cultural ambassadors to the world," a title the members carry with them with the highest honor. In 2018 the group received not one but two GRAMMY Award nominations for two separate albums, a first in the history of the World Music award category. These two nominations brought their career total to 19 GRAMMY Award nominations. One of these albums, Shaka Zulu Revisited , won Best World Music Album. Ladysmith Black Mambazo continues to tour the globe and has performed for millions of people, singing a message of peace, love, and harmony. ev_eb8b74842789.description: Lynne Maes, rhythm guitar & vocals; Hank Maninger, lead guitar & vocals; Tim Wagar, bass guitar; Paul Revelli drums You're in for two sets in honky tonk heaven. Mainstays of the Bay Area Americana scene, and the Bird & Beckett bandstand, for nearly a decade, Nashville Honeymoon has traversed country, rockabilly, bluegrass, and pop across four albums, writing songs that uplift the tangled mess of day-to-day life and investigate universal themes of love and loss – often at the same time. Their latest album, Sidewinder, is true to its title, offering a collection of songs that are grounded in classic country while edging into different sounds, genres, and themes that run through American pop music. This is some of the sweetest, sauciest, and most sincere country music you'll ever hear. SUNDAY HAPPY HOUR! Grab your partner! Gather your kids! Call a friend! Come on down to the bookshop to get a bit better acquainted with your neighbors and just have a ball before the start of another long hard work week!

Doctorow, Ramon is offered a promotion and cash which could pay for grad school – if he agrees to enter a green-card marriage with his boss's niece. When he agrees, he gets more than he bargained for. "Smoke and Shadows" by Tatyana Tolstaya centers on a Russian professor living in the U.S., navigating her professional life, her intimate relationships, and the mysteries of culture. ev_f1957ea40615.description: Skylar Tang is a multidisciplinary musician from the San Francisco Bay Area known for her dynamic trumpet playing and profound compositions. Tang has shared the stage with world-renowned artists such as Sean Jones, Dee Dee Bridgewater, Rufus Reid, and Joshua Redman. She was featured on Redman's latest album, Words Fall Short . Now based in New York City, Tang attends Columbia University and The Juilliard School studying History and Jazz Performance. As a bandleader and composer, Tang seeks to capture the moments in our lives where we feel truly present. Her thoughtful writing and her quartet's elegant delivery cultivate an atmosphere that welcomes and affirms the listener. ev_f1be2ce2b417.description: Angie Minkin and Heather Saunders Estes both have new poetry collections out: LineageSongs and Crosswinds , respectively. Come hear their poems, and bring one of your own for the open mic to follow. From rolling the dice, sliding down chutes, climbing the ladders of memory, or shooting free throws for the departed, Angie Minkin's Lineage Songs takes us on a journey where the poet speaks of love and kinship in the shadow of roosters who lack alarm clocks and any decent sense of timing. We zigzag from inner to outer world, consider dreams of "prowling jaguars and river-drinking deer" and dance through an examined life as the poems question the status quo of what we believe, war, how we live with ourselves, and, finally, how we reclaim our own loving presence and ancestry in this complicated world. Michael Koch and Jerry Ferraz are your hosts and m.c.s No charge to attend or read. Donations appreciated to help us compensate the featured poets. POETS! Every 1st Thursday, featured readers followed by a community open mic.

ev_f5de1078fe8a.description: The Garage Jam is an open, friendly bluegrass circle that meets the first and third Monday of every month, from 6 to 8 pm. All kinds of pickers show up, from rank beginners to grizzled veterans, plus folks who just come to listen and socialize. The repertoire is straight-up traditional bluegrass, although the occasional old-time or folk-inflected choice will pop up. The format is the old-fashioned song circle, with each participant getting a turn to call a song and set its key, pace, and feel. An experienced jam leader and bass player are always present to help keep things on track. Everyone is welcome — come on down!

ev_f728dfbc0eb5.description: The Bad Plus are the ultimate originals, and this Farewell Tour features the band's final performances, celebrating their twenty-six years of musical collaboration and influence. A democratic unit with a clear vision and a refusal to conform to convention, for the past two decades The Bad Plus have played with spirit and adventure, made their own rules and done so with a bold sense of creativity and intent. Avoiding easy categorization, The Bad Plus has won critical acclaim and a legion of fans worldwide with their unique sound and flair for live performance. The Bad Plus continue to push boundaries as founding members Reid Anderson (bass) and Dave King (drums) embark on a new piano-less incarnation of the band with Ben Monder (guitar) and Chris Speed (tenor saxophone) – instigating a new wave of excitement and anticipation within the band that is re-energizing their sound and inspiration. The Bad Plus have constantly searched to bridge genres and techniques while exploring the infinite possibilities of exceptional musicians working in perfect sync. The Bad Plus Website Sponsored by Lighthouse Realty, Krista and Peter Cook (Ticket Includes 5% City of Santa Cruz Admission Tax) .embe

Doctorow & Tatyana Tolstaya Presented by Word for Word and Z Space Directed by Rotimi Agbabiaka In "Assimilation" by E. L. Doctorow, Ramon is offered a promotion and cash which could pay for grad school – if he agrees to enter a green-card marriage with his boss's niece. When he agrees, he gets more than he bargained for. "Smoke and Shadows" by Tatyana Tolstaya centers on a Russian professor living in the U.S., navigating her professional life, her intimate relationships, and the mysteries of culture. Told with Tolstaya's sharp, restrained wit, the story zeros in on the experience of living in a new culture, and the confusions and imbalance that can cause. What does it mean to assimilate? These two writers offer two very different perspectives. ev_fa3378259d50.description: In the mid 1990s, The New York Times described Larry Goldings , Peter Bernstein , and Bill Stewart as "the best organ trio of the last decade." The trio, which has now been together for over thirty years, has been recognized for charting new ground, with its synergistic playing and thoughtful music. They have released over a dozen recordings, all of which display their distinctive sound, whether exploring the depths of jazz standards, or playing their own original compositions. Of their latest offering, Toy Tunes , DownBeat said, "The whole album subtly subverts organ-trio cliches, offering not chicken-shack party stomps but instead some hip after-hours atmospherics...". The Goldings/Bernstein/Stewart Organ Trio will feature Goldings on organ, Bernstein on guitar, and Stewart on drums. ev_fc34801cb484.description: French acoustic guitar virtuoso, vocalist, and composer Pierre Bensusan , surnamed "Mister DADGAD", has taken his unique sound to all corners of the globe. Winner of the Independent Music Award for his triple live album "Encore", voted Best World Music Guitarist by Guitar Player Magazine readers' Poll, winner of the Rose d'Or at the Montreux Festival for his debut album, Pierre is recognized as one of the greatest guitar players of the 21st century. When Michael Hedges titles one of his compositions "Bensusan", you know that the inspiration behind it must be special, and Pierre Bensusan certainly is. Guitarists from Leo Kottke to Larry Corryel, to Tuck Andress, Tommy Emmanuel, Mark Knopfler, Andrew York, Andy Timmons, Pat Metheny, and Steve Lukather... have sung his praises, and Steve Vai released three Bensusan albums on his label Favored Nations. And it's not just guitarists who are so inspired by Pierre's music, as a recent studio collaboration with him on Donny Osmond's latest album "Start Again" goes to show. If World Music means the fusion of traditional, contemporary, jazz, classical, and pop music, then Bensusan is one of the most eloquent World Music musicians of our time.

ev_fe42f85bca82.description: Naima Shalhoub, voice/keyboards; Scott Oshiro, flute/quantum electronics; Alex Heigl, guitar/effects; Chris Trinidad, bass/guitar/synth/bass; Cy Thompson, drums/percussion Chris Trinidad's latest project Chroma Tonic weaves together musicians from wildly divergent backgrounds in order to concoct unique sounds and intriguing groove music. Drawing inspiration from ambient music pioneers Brian Eno and Robert Fripp, the early avant-garde space psychedelia of Pink Floyd, the progressive electronic rock of Tu-Ner, the adventurous electric hybrid experimentations of early seventies Miles Davis, Chris Trinidad's Chroma Tonic blends these explorations with the influences of the members of the group. Naima Shalhoub provides vocal and synthesizer textures, Alex Heigl plays ambient and looped guitars, Cy Thompson brings an array of Afro-Caribbean percussive elements, Scott Oshiro performs on flute and programs the quantum (!!) electronic improvised live interactions, while Chris Trinidad holds down the foundation on bass guitar and synth bass. $25 cover charge; byob Students $10 For a reservation, call the bookshop at 415-586-3733

ev_ff5098fc4518.description: Pipo Romero is a composer and guitarist from Cádiz who has captivated the international scene. His innovative spanish acoustic fingerstyle blends influences from flamenco and folk traditions from various cultures, creating a unique sound praised by critics and audiences alike. His compositions offer a rich and emotional experience that transcends cultural boundaries, establishing him as one of the most innovative figures in the acoustic guitar world.
